title: fix database locking issues in macOS app
description:
SQLite database is getting locked when bd CLI writes while app reads.

Solutions:
1. Add retry logic with exponential backoff for SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED errors
2. Use WAL mode (Write-Ahead Logging) for better concurrency
3. Set busy timeout on SQLite connections
4. Consider read-only connections where possible

title: fix macOS app sync to match CLI approach
description:
Problems with current macOS app sync:
1. Uses random UUID for source ID instead of deterministic path-based ID
2. Has unnecessary "registration" step that's failing with HTTP 500
3. Doesn't match CLI sync daemon approach

Fix:
- Remove registration step from macOS app
- Use same source ID generation as CLI (base64 encoded path)
- Just push issues directly like CLI does
- Source gets created/updated automatically on first push

CLI reference: src/sync/Sources/CloudAPI.swift:82-89

title: implement notifications for tasks closed by others

- compare before/after to detect status transitions
- get device_id from API to identify who made changes
- detect if change was made by current device or another
- send notification when status changes to closed by someone else
- notification format: 'Issue closed: [title]' with details about who closed it

implementation:
- extend pullAndApplyChanges() to track state changes
- add device ID to SyncDaemon (maybe from API or generate locally)
- compare changes and filter for status transitions to closed
- check device_tracking from API to see if it was us
- call sendNotification() for remote closures
- maybe add notification preferences in settings

note: SyncDaemon already uses bd CLI in applyChange() - should refactor to direct JSONL write like we did in IssueStore

- use in all API calls for device_tracking

title: detect issue status transitions in sync
description:
track issue state before/after sync to detect status changes

implementation:
- in pullAndApplyChanges, snapshot current issues before pulling
- create beforeMap: [id: Issue] for quick lookup
- compare each changed issue with before state
- detect status transitions (especially to closed)
- return list of IssueTransition objects
- prepare for notification logic
notes: snapshot issue states before pulling changes - compare with pulled changes to detect transitions - focus on status changes to closed - check if updated_by_device_id matches our device - only notify for changes from other devices - see docs/TRANSITION_NOTIFICATIONS.md and docs/FEATURES/DEVICE_TRACKING.md
